steps.text: Place zucchini and onion in a large, non-metallic bowl; sprinkle salt on top. Use your hands to evenly mix salt with zucchini. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Drain zucchini in a colander and rinse well with cool water. Squeeze out excess water; set zucchini aside.

Place sugar, vinegar, red and green bell pepper, and cornstarch into a large pot. Add celery seed, nutmeg, turmeric, and black pepper. Stir to combine, then add drained zucchini. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat; reduce heat to medium-low and simmer 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, sterilize seven 1-pint jars and lids. Pack relish into sterilized jars, filling to within 1/4 inch of the top. Screw on the lids.

Place a rack in the bottom of a large stockpot and fill halfway with boiling water. Carefully lower jars into the pot using a holder. Leave a 2-inch space between jars. Pour in more boiling water if necessary, until the tops of jars are covered by 2 inches of water. Bring water to a full boil, then cover and process for 30 minutes.

Remove jars from the pot and place on a cloth-covered or wood surface, several inches apart, until cool. Once cool, press the top of each lid with a finger, ensuring that seal is tight (lid does not move up or down at all).

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Zucchini Relish
raw_recipe.description: This zucchini relish with green and red bell peppers is flavored with nutmeg and turmeric. It’s delicious on hamburgers, hot dogs, or whatever you like!

review.reviewBody: I have made a similiar recipe for about 20 years now. Once you have tried this relish you never want to go back to store bought. The difference between this recipe & mine is.. I use apple cider vinegar, 4 cups sugar, 1 TBSLP dry mustard & 1/8 cayenne pepper and a 2 tsp. cornstarch. I found mine just perfect for sweetness. So, to all you relish users..... try it...You'll love it!!!!

I adapted this recipie and used my B&B Zucchini process technique - - shred the Zukes, prep the onions, add the two together then toss with the salt. Cover the mixture with a layer of ice cubes, cover the bowl, and then place in the refidgerator. Chill for 3 - 6 hrs. I did not find any need to go the full overnight method. 

Substituted Apple Cider Vinegar and added 1 Tablespoon slightly cracked Mustard Seed, reduced Sugar to 2 cups, omitted the Corn Starch, added 2 diced red Jalapeno peppers . If you really want it thicker - I suggest Clear Gel - a modified starch for canning and pie fillings. Clear Gel is just that, clear, no clouding and very reasonable. - this is wonderful and the acidity is safe per my Ph Paper test.

I decreased the sugar to 3 cups (not 6) the first time I made it, and the relish tastes just like Willies zucchini relish, which is no longer available on the market. This year, I'm trying it with just 2 cups sugar, but I can say for sure that half the sugar and all the rest as directed made the best zucchini relish I've ever had. The hardest part was sterilizing the jars, I tried 3 times to do it with boiling the jars but our hard water left a white film on the jars. So I would recommend that you wash the jars and put them in the oven , bake at 230F for 20 minutes to sterilize them instead.

This recipe is spectacular! Great way to use up all of that zucchini from the garden. You absolutely can safely adjust the sugar content to half, since this recipe is almost identical to the zesty zucchini relish in the Ball Complete Book of Home Preserving (2006), which uses 2 1/2 cups sugar and all of the same base ingredients and same quantities as this recipe. Also according to ball, use 1/2 inch headspace. The only other difference is some spices.

I just made a batch based off of this recipe but made a few adjustments. I used 3 cups of sugar, apple Cider vinegar, my two bell peppers were smaller so I also added two Mad Hatters and 6 Jalapeños (kept seeds from two of them) also 1/2 teaspoon of dry mustard powder and tossed in a spice ball of pickling spice. The relish came out perfectly sweet with just a little heat. I have a feeling I will be making this again. This only yielded approximately 60oz nearly half of what we were expecting.
Very good recipe, made again with half sugar and 1 tbsp. mustard seed. Couldn't tell sugar difference and mustard seed was also a great add on for our tastes

I added a cup less sugar as i thought it was too much. I tasted it before i jarred it and i would probably cut it back again. The quantities i had called for 4 cups but 2 1/2 i think would be plenty. Also we will see how thick it is. My recipe called for 2 1/2 tsp of corn starch but another similar recipe called for 4 tsp. So i will have to wait and see how it turns out once it is cooled. But the taste was great!! Would make again!

I have made this recipe for more than 5 years, after receiving a jar of zucchini relish as gift at a wedding I attended. I found this recipe to taste exactly like the relish I was given. So very good! I see on other's posting that others safely reduced the sugar amount by as much as half, and similar to Ball's Zesty relish. I reduced mine by 1 1/4 cup and it is sweet enough. I add a Tbsp. or 2 to potato salad and it makes it even better!
Made it and loved it! My mods are as follows: added 1 tbsp mustard seed, reduced to 4 cups sugar, substituted 1/2 cup ACV, added 1/4 tsp cayenne pepper. This made 9 x 250ml jars
I too cut the sugar in half, added a few more red peppers and 2 teaspoons of dry mustard. Also used half apple cider/regular vinegar. Very good.

The recipe itself tastes wonderful, but as another reviewer has pointed out, the recipe does not use best practices for canning and should be ignored. Relishes should have 1/2" headspace at the top, not be completely filled as described, and the rims should be inspected and cleaned before sealing. I recommend researching proper canning techniques and following those instead of what is listed here verbatim.

Everyone who has tried my relish loves it. I make a variation of this recipe every year. The quantities, except for the sugar are accurate. There is no need to put almost a cup of sugar in every pint jar. I follow everything else for the most part. Whatever peppers are on hand go into the pot. Its great if you throw in a couple of chili peppers or jalapenos. The recipe is very forgiving so as long as you have enough acid to preserve.

I've made a double batch, it's good but way too sweet. I reduced the sugar to 8 cups instead of the 12, and it's still too sweet. I know the sugar is part of preservation but can a person just do half the sugar

I made a half batch. I used yellow bell pepper, and didn't add the celery seed.( I just didn't have any. This was a really easy recipe and tasted great. I will definitely keep using this recipe. Thank you for submitting it.
Delicious! Tastes just like the zucchini relish my mom used to make! Sweet memories! Thank you!!!
Love this relish. I made some towards the end of the season last year and was sorry I hadn’t made more. This year I’ll definitely make extra.
This is super easy & yummy.
My husband could not say enough good things about this recipe. We did add a little bit more cornstarch for thickness.
Love it, love it, love it.This is my second year of making it.I kicked up a notch.I added celery and a yellow pepper and carrot for color👍👍❤️❤️😃🤗
Good flavor excellent in tuna salad!
